chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Azrami, who said:

Muawiya appointed Marwan ibn al-Hakam over Medina and ordered him to assign stipends for the youth of Quraysh, so he assigned them. Then Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: 'So I went to him, and he said,

Then he assigned a stipend for me. So I returned to my father and informed him. He said: 'Woe to the son of al-Zarqa, the tanner of the unseeded land. If a hundred were born to me, I would love that I not name any of them except Ali.'

key_terms.ابْنُ الزَّرْقَاءِ: The son of al-Zarqa (a nickname for Marwan)
key_terms.دَبَّاغَةِ الْأَدَمِ: The tanner of the unseeded land (a derogatory epithet)
key_terms.شَبَابِ قُرَيْشٍ: The youth of the Quraysh tribe
key_terms.مَرْوَانُ بْنُ الْحَكَمِ: Marwan ibn al-Hakam, a Umayyad governor

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Ali name all his sons Ali according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the distinctive Shia practice of naming all male descendants 'Ali' to emulate the first Imam, a tradition rooted in the Umayyad era as evidenced by Marwan ibn al-Hakam’s inquiry. The Imam’s response underscores the spiritual significance of the name, linking it to the Prophet’s lineage and divine favor, while his subsequent blessing for his son reflects the enduring reverence for Ali ibn Abi Talib in Shia theology.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Barqy, from Abdul Rahman Bin Muhammad Al Azramy who said,

‘Muawiya (appointed) Marwan Bin Al-Hakam as an office bearer at Al-Medina, and instructed him that he should impose upon the youth of Qureysh, so he imposed to them. So Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So he came over to me<sup>asws</sup>, so he said, ‘What is your<sup>asws</sup> name?’ So I said, ‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>’. So he said, ‘What is the name of your<sup>asws</sup> brother?’ So I<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Ali’. So he said, ‘Ali and Ali, what did your<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> intend, that he<sup>asws</sup> did not leave anyone from his<sup>asws</sup> sons except that he<sup>asws</sup> named him as Ali?’

Then he imposed to me. So I<sup>asws</sup> returned to my<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup>, so I<sup>asws</sup> informed him<sup>asws</sup>. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Woe be unto the son of Zarqa, the tanner of the unseeded land. If there were born for me<sup>asws</sup> one hundred (sons), I<sup>asws</sup> would love it not to name anyone of them except as Ali’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad formal-Barqiy from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-‘Arzamiy who has said the following:

“Mu‘awiyah appointed Marwan ibn al-Hakam as his agent in al-Madinah and ordered him to pay a certain salary to the young people of Quraysh which he did. Ali ibn al-Husayn, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, has said, ‘I went to him and he asked, ‘What is your name?’ I replied, ‘It is Ali ibn al-Husayn.’ He then asked, ‘What is the name of your brother?’ I replied, ‘It is Ali.’ He said, ‘Ali and Ali. Is it that your father does not want to leave any of his children without naming them all Ali?’

He paid me a certain amount. I returned to my father and informed him of what had happened. He (the Imam) said, ‘Woe is upon the son of al-Zarqa’, the leather- treating man. Even if one hundred sons will be born to me I will not give anyone of them any other name except Ali.’”
